name: F5 iApp APL
comment: APL — the presentation language of an F5 iApp template. Not Tcl: it has its own grammar of sections, typed fields and attributes, with `[ … ]` bracket expressions that *are* Tcl. Every Tcl-family language used to be pointed at `tcl.tmLanguage.json`, which contains no APL rule at all, so an APL file was painted with Tcl rules until the server answered and replaced them wholesale (issue #903). The scopes below are the ones `package.json` already maps the server's `apl*` semantic-token types to, so the static paint and the semantic paint agree instead of contradicting each other. Where the grammar cannot tell (a bareword that is a field *name* only because of its position), it emits nothing rather than guess wrong.

directive.comment: A preprocessor directive. Matched before #comment so `#include` is not swallowed as one.

embedded-tcl.comment: A bracket expression is Tcl, and the server walks it as Tcl. Painting it as Tcl here keeps the two layers in step.

field.comment: A field declaration is `<field-type> <name> …`. The type word identifies it, so the name that follows can be scoped too — that positional fact is the one thing a static grammar *can* know here.

validator.comment: The validators APL ships with, named inside `validator "…"`. The whole construct is matched as one unit, quotes included: TextMate resolves competing patterns by which one starts *earliest*, not by list order, so the opening quote would otherwise start #string and the name inside would be painted as ordinary string content. Only a name in this position is a validator — a bare `Number` elsewhere is not.
